settlement_source: Multi-source: Israeli official gazette/government websites, office of head of state, Knesset, plus Reuters, AP, BBC, NYT, FT, Bloomberg, Guardian, WaPo, major Israeli news (Kalshi metadata lists a parliament.go.ke URL for the legislature - Kenya, metadata error)
settlement_variable: Identity of first person formally appointed/invested as Israeli PM (full powers, non-caretaker) via government formation after the 2026 Israeli legislative election, before Oct 27 2027
tie_handling: n/a; first person to meet ALL criteria; rotating PM -> first to assume office
trading_close_vs_settlement: Last trading = expiration (latest 2027-10-27 10:00 ET) but resolves earlier when event occurs (Rule 7.2); accelerated resolution if >=2 of 6 designated international media (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC, Bloomberg, NYT) unambiguously state a winner
early_close_or_void_clauses: No government by Oct 27 2027 -> No one (if option) else No for all. New elections before formation -> No one immediately. Death of leader -> last fair price for that market, successor may be Yes. Non-listed person -> Other. Sole-discretion outcome review. can_close_early=1.
title_vs_rules_divergences: Title Who will be PM after the election vs rules: must be formally invested; designate, largest-party leader, or caretaker do not count (incumbent caretaker status irrelevant)
Accelerated resolution triggers on media statements that a candidate has won - may fire before formal investiture; ambiguity
Death clause pays last fair price (discretionary) rather than binary
Election date itself not in title (ticker suggests 26OCT27 - unverified)

toxicity_flags: Election-night exit polls/counts public well before investiture; fast news reprices, slow quoting adversely selected
Coalition negotiations opaque; Hebrew-press leaks precede English wires
Very long dated (~12 months): capital lockup and resolution timing uncertainty
Source metadata error (legislature URL points to Kenya)
Kalshi discretionary review; Other/No one option structure
notes: High volume (3.6M 24h). Source pages and election date not independently verified. Feed latencies from general knowledge.
